landing.tagline: Manage your Discord server from a modern web dashboard.
landing.description: Welcome messages, moderation, roles, tickets, levels and much more. Configured per server, no commands needed.
landing.feature1Body: Every module is configured with forms and a live preview.
landing.feature2Body: Independent settings for every community you manage.
landing.feature3Body: Only people who can manage the server can change anything.

loginError.state: The sign-in expired. Please try again.
loginError.discord: Discord didn't respond. Please try again.

login.notConfigured: The Discord application is not configured in the .env file (DISCORD_CLIENT_ID and DISCORD_CLIENT_SECRET).

servers.title: Your servers
servers.subtitle: Pick a server to configure it.
servers.emptyBody: You need the Manage Server permission on Discord to configure a server.

alerts.missing_intent: The “{intent}” intent must be enabled in the Developer Portal.
alerts.bot_cannot_send: NEXUS can't send messages in a configured channel.

permissions.description: Give dashboard access to roles in your server without making them admins.
permissions.managersNote: People with “Manage Server” or “Administrator” in Discord always have full access. Only they can change this page.
permissions.levelsHelp: View: read only · Edit: save changes · Manage: enable/disable and delete.
permissions.emptyBody: Add a role to give it dashboard access.

settings.title: Settings
settings.description: General NEXUS settings for this server.
settings.localeHelp: Language of the bot's messages and replies.
settings.timezoneHelp: Used for scheduled messages and dates. Current time: {time}
settings.embedColorHelp: Color of the side bar on the bot's messages.
settings.invalidColor: Use a 6-digit HEX color, for example #7465F7.

diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
diagnostics.description: Check that NEXUS has everything it needs in this server.
diagnostics.allGood: All good. NEXUS has the permissions it needs.
diagnostics.hierarchyBody: NEXUS can only give or remove roles below its own role. If a role module doesn't work, move the NEXUS role up in Server Settings → Roles.

audit.title: History
audit.description: Changes made to this server's configuration.

soonPage.title: {name} is coming soon
soonPage.body: This module is planned for phase {phase}. Meanwhile, you can configure the available modules.

account.title: My account
account.deleteBody: Deletes your dashboard account, sessions and Discord tokens. Server configurations are not deleted.

states.apiDown: The API isn't responding. Is it running on port 8000?
states.readOnly: Read only: you need the manage permission to save changes.
states.botOffline: NEXUS is offline. You can edit, but changes will apply when it comes back.
states.botMissingBody: Invite the bot to configure this server. You'll come back here when you're done.
states.noAccessTitle: You don't have access to this section
states.noAccessBody: Your roles don't have permission for this part of the panel. If you need it, ask an admin to grant it in Advanced → Permissions.
states.notFoundBody: The page you're looking for doesn't exist.

save.errors: {count, plural, one {# field has errors} other {# fields have errors}}
save.conflictBody: Someone saved this configuration while you were editing. You can view their changes (losing yours) or overwrite them.
save.leaveBody: Changes you haven't saved will be lost.

editor.author: Author
editor.title: Title

editor.warn_channel_not_found: Saved, but the chosen channel no longer exists.

welcome.description: Greet new members and say goodbye to those who leave.
welcome.sendJoinHelp: Sent when someone joins the server.
welcome.sendLeaveHelp: Sent when someone leaves the server.
welcome.channelRequired: Pick a channel to send the message to.
welcome.messageHelp: Use variables like '{'user'}' or '{'server'}'; they are replaced when sending.
welcome.dmHelp: Besides the channel message, NEXUS can DM the new member.
welcome.testDm: Send me the test by DM
welcome.testHelp: Sends the saved configuration using you as the new member.
welcome.saveFirst: Save your changes before sending the test.
welcome.err_bot_cannot_send: NEXUS can't send messages in that channel. Check its permissions.
welcome.err_dm_closed: I couldn't DM you. Are your direct messages closed?

embeds.description: Build a message with an embed and send it to any channel.
embeds.help: The draft is saved in this browser until you press «New message». Sent messages don't mention anyone.
embeds.newBody: What's in the editor will be cleared. Messages you already sent don't change.
embeds.afterSend: The message stays in the editor in case you want to send it to another channel or make a similar one.

module.disabledNotice: This module is disabled: changes are saved, but NEXUS won't apply them until you enable it.
module.permsMissing: NEXUS is missing permissions for this module: {perms}. Give them to NEXUS's role in Server Settings → Roles, or re-invite it.

moderation.description: Moderation commands, case history and automatic punishments.
moderation.logChannelHelp: Every punishment is posted here. If empty, the Logs → Moderation channel is used.
moderation.dmOnActionHelp: Sends them the reason and duration.
moderation.requireReasonHelp: Commands fail if no reason is given.
moderation.warnExpiryHelp: Expired warnings don't count toward automatic punishments.
moderation.banDeleteDays: When banning, delete messages from the last
moderation.escalationHelp: What happens when active warnings add up.
moderation.duplicateWarns: Two steps have the same number of warnings.
moderation.commandsHelp: Commands: /warn, /timeout (e.g. 1h = {example}), /kick, /ban, /unban, /softban, /warnings, /case, /note, /pardon, /clearwarns, /purge, /slowmode, /lock, /unlock. Only people with the matching Discord permission can see them.
moderation.noCasesBody: Punishments from commands or AutoMod will show up here.

automod.description: Detects and stops spam, links, slurs and more without staff action.
automod.rulesHelp: Checked by priority; the first match applies. Staff with “Manage messages” are not moderated.
automod.noRulesBody: Create a rule to get started. We recommend enabling it in test mode first.
automod.logChannelHelp: Every detection is reported here. Empty = Logs → Moderation channel.
automod.deleteBody: The rule will stop applying immediately.
automod.name: Name
automod.help_spam: Too many messages in a short time.
automod.help_duplicates: The same message repeated several times.
automod.help_bad_words: One word per line. Use * as a wildcard (spam* blocks spammer). Also catches tricks like 4 for a or 0 for o.
automod.help_links: Controls which domains can be linked.
automod.help_invites: Blocks invites to other Discord servers.
automod.help_mass_mentions: Too many mentions in one message.
automod.help_caps: Messages written almost entirely in caps.
automod.domainsHelp: One per line, e.g. youtube.com (subdomains included).
automod.testModeHelp: Only alerts; doesn't delete or punish.
automod.tryHelp: Type a message to see which rule would catch it.
automod.tryNote: Spam and repeated messages depend on timing and can't be tried here.

logging.description: Log what happens in the server to the channels you choose.
logging.catHelp_messages: Deleted and edited messages (needs the Message Content intent).
logging.ignoredHelp: Messages from these channels aren't logged.
logging.privacy: Message content is sent to the log channel and isn't stored in the NEXUS database.
logging.catHelp_voice: Voice joins, leaves and channel switches, with how long each person stayed.
logging.whereHelp: Summary of every notice in the server. Click one to change it.

autoroles.description: Automatically give roles to people who join the server.
autoroles.botsHelp: Roles for bots that are added.
autoroles.waitScreeningHelp: If the server uses Membership Screening, roles are given after accepting.
autoroles.delayHelp: Useful against accounts that join and leave right away.
autoroles.hierarchy: NEXUS can't give these roles because they're above its own: {roles}. Move the NEXUS role up in Server Settings → Roles.

rr.description: Panels where members pick their roles with buttons, a menu or reactions.
rr.defaultMessage: Press a button to add or remove the role.
rr.emptyBody: Create a panel and publish it to a channel.
rr.deleteBody: The panel message in Discord will also be deleted.
rr.modeHelp_normal: Each option adds or removes its role.
rr.modeHelp_unique: Only one role from the panel at a time.
rr.modeHelp_verify: Only adds roles; they can't be removed from the panel.
rr.label: Text
rr.channelLocked: To change the channel, delete the panel and create it again.

members.description: Find members, review their history and moderate from the dashboard.
members.activeWarns: {count, plural, one {# active warning} other {# active warnings}}
members.actionHelp: NEXUS runs the action with the same rules as the commands (hierarchy, DM notice and automatic punishments).

tickets.description: Private support channels members open with a button.
tickets.panelsHelp: Each panel is a message with a button to open tickets. Up to 5.
tickets.openingHelp: Sent inside the ticket. You can use variables like '{'user'}'.
tickets.askSubject: Ask for a subject when opening
tickets.transcriptsHelp: When a ticket closes, its history is sent here as an HTML file.
tickets.dmTranscript: Send the transcript to the creator

suggestions.description: Members propose ideas with /suggest and vote with buttons.
suggestions.staffHelp: In addition to people with “Manage messages”.
suggestions.noneBody: They'll show up when someone uses /suggest.

starboard.description: Highlight the most-reacted messages in a special channel.
starboard.help: When a message gets {count} {emoji} reactions, it's copied to the starboard channel.

polls.description: Native Discord polls: members vote and see results instantly.
polls.newHelp: Posted as an official Discord poll.
polls.question: Question
polls.commandHelp: If off, only people with “Manage messages” can create polls with /poll.

giveaways.description: Giveaways with an enter button, role requirements and verifiable winners.
giveaways.managersHelp: Can use /giveaway in addition to people with “Manage Server”.
giveaways.seedHelp: Giveaway seed: with it and the entry list you can verify the winners were picked at random.

commands.description: Create your own slash commands: they reply with a message and can add or remove roles.
commands.help: Changes take a few seconds to show up in Discord. They don't run code: they only reply and manage roles.
commands.deleteBody: The command will disappear from Discord.
commands.name: Name
commands.ephemeral: Private reply (only the user sees it)
commands.err_name_taken: A command with that name already exists.

scheduled.description: Post announcements now or schedule them (once or repeating). Times are in your time zone: {tz}.
scheduled.noneBody: Create an announcement and choose when to post it.
scheduled.mentionsNote: These messages can mention @everyone and roles if you write them in the text.

levels.description: Members earn experience by chatting, level up and unlock roles.
levels.xpHelp: Random XP per message, at most once per interval.
levels.xpError: Min can't be greater than max.
levels.rewardsHelp: Roles given when reaching each level.
levels.resetBody: They'll go back to level 0. Roles already given are kept.

economy.description: The server's virtual currency: daily rewards, jobs, transfers and a shop.
economy.earningHelp: /daily and /work commands, plus an optional reward per message.
economy.workError: Minimum can't be greater than maximum.
economy.adjustHelp: Give or take coins from a member. It's logged.
economy.amountHelp: Negative to take. Balance never goes below 0.
economy.disclaimer: These are virtual points with no real value: they can't be bought with money or exchanged for anything outside the server.

integrations.description: Announce new videos, live streams, articles or releases in Discord.
integrations.noneBody: Add a YouTube channel, a Twitch streamer, an RSS feed or a GitHub repository.
integrations.deleteBody: Notifications from this source will stop.
integrations.twitchMissing: For Twitch notifications, add TWITCH_CLIENT_ID and TWITCH_CLIENT_SECRET to .env (free app at dev.twitch.tv).
integrations.howItWorks: NEXUS checks YouTube, RSS and GitHub every 5 minutes and Twitch every 2. Adding a source doesn't announce what was already published; only new items.
integrations.sourceHelp_youtube: Channel link with /channel/UC… or the ID starting with UC.
integrations.sourceHelp_rss: Address of the RSS or Atom feed.
integrations.sourceHelp_github: owner/repository or the link. Announces new releases.
integrations.varsHelp: Variables: '{'title'}', '{'url'}', '{'author'}', '{'name'}' and '{'thumbnail'}' plus the usual ones.
integrations.err_youtube_channel_id_required: Use the link with /channel/UC… (on YouTube: About → Share channel → Copy channel ID).
integrations.err_private_address: That address points to a private network and isn't allowed.
integrations.err_invalid_feed: The address isn't a valid RSS or Atom feed.
integrations.err_twitch_not_configured: Twitch isn't configured on the server.
integrations.err_redirect_not_allowed: The address redirects elsewhere: use the final address.
integrations.err_bot_cannot_send: NEXUS can't write in the chosen channel.

ai.description: Claude reviews messages and catches scams, harassment or spam that fixed rules miss. Always with human review.
ai.notConfigured: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is missing from .env: the AI won't review messages until you add it.
ai.privacy: Privacy: only the message text and your rules are sent to Anthropic, never names or IDs. NEXUS doesn't store the text. Let your community know in your rules or privacy policy.
ai.rulesHelp: The AI uses them for the “Against server rules” category.
ai.thresholdError: The review threshold can't be above the action threshold.
ai.requests: {count, plural, one {# review} other {# reviews}} this month
ai.limitHelp: When reached, the AI pauses until next month.

analytics.description: How your community evolves: growth, activity and moderation.
analytics.noMod: No moderation actions in this period.

setup.title: Quick setup
setup.description: Pick your community type and NEXUS enables and configures the recommended modules in three steps.
setup.tplDesc_gaming: Welcomes, interest roles, levels, giveaways and auto-moderation.
setup.tplDesc_support: Tickets, suggestions, logs and moderation with required reasons.
setup.tplDesc_creator: YouTube/Twitch alerts, scheduled announcements, giveaways and levels.
setup.tplDesc_study: Subject roles, levels, polls and reminders.
setup.tplDesc_professional: Strict moderation, AutoMod and full logging.
setup.pickModules: Turn off what you don't want. Everything can be changed later.
setup.pickChannels: Choose where NEXUS will post. You can leave fields empty and set them later.
setup.noChannels: The chosen modules don't need a channel.
setup.overwriteHelp: If on, their configuration is replaced by the template's. If off, they're only enabled without changes.
setup.afterwards: Afterwards you can fine-tune each module from the sidebar.
setup.done: {count, plural, one {# module configured} other {# modules configured}}
setup.overviewHint: No modules are active yet. Quick setup gets the server ready in a minute.

antiraid.description: Protect the server from raids and fake accounts: verification on join, new accounts, mass-join detection and quarantine.
antiraid.verificationHelp: New members press a button (and answer a sum, if you pick captcha) to get the access role.
antiraid.verifyIncomplete: Pick the channel and role to enable verification.
antiraid.setupTitle: How to set it up in Discord
antiraid.setup1: Create a "Verified" role below NEXUS's role.
antiraid.setup2: Pick below which channels are visible without verifying and press "Apply restriction".
antiraid.setup3: Keep the verification channel visible to @everyone and publish the panel.
antiraid.youngHelp: Detect freshly created accounts, typical of raids and alts.
antiraid.needQuarantineRole: To use quarantine, pick or create the quarantine role below.
antiraid.raidHelp: If many accounts join at once, NEXUS reacts on its own and alerts staff.
antiraid.raidSummary: Triggers if {joins} accounts join within {seconds} seconds. To go back to normal: /raidmode on:False.
antiraid.alertsHelp: Where NEXUS alerts and which role it uses to isolate suspicious members.
antiraid.quarantineRoleHelp: A role that can't see any channel.
antiraid.roleCreated: Role created and hidden in {count} channels. Save your changes.
antiraid.gateHelp: New members only see the channels you pick (plus the verification one). Once verified, they see the rest.
antiraid.publicHelp: For example #rules or #welcome. The verification channel is always included. Max 10.
antiraid.gateRule1: Private channels (staff, tickets, logs) are left untouched.
antiraid.gateRule2: Previous permissions are saved: you can undo it with one click.
antiraid.gateRule3: New channels you create inside a hidden category will be hidden too.
antiraid.gateApplyBody: NEXUS will change your channel permissions: @everyone will stop seeing all channels except the public ones, and the verified role will see them. Current permissions are saved so you can undo it.
antiraid.gateUndoBody: Your channel permissions will go back exactly to how they were before applying the restriction.
antiraid.gateRemoved: Restriction removed: permissions are back to how they were.
antiraid.gateNeedsVerify: Enable and save verification (channel and role) first.

tempvoice.description: Members join "➕ Create room" and NEXUS creates their own voice room, deleted automatically when empty.
tempvoice.hubHelp: Voice channel: joining it creates the room.
tempvoice.limitHelp: 0 = no limit. The owner can change it with /voice limit.
tempvoice.quickHelp: Creates a "🔊 Temporary rooms" category with a "➕ Create room" channel and fills them in here.
tempvoice.how: Each room owner controls it with /voice:
tempvoice.commands: lock · unlock · limit · name · permit · reject · claim · bitrate

voice.description: Records who joins voice channels, how long they stay and which channels. Only who, where and how long is stored: never audio.
voice.historyHelp: The 50 most recent sessions. Click a name to see only theirs.
voice.emptyBody: When someone joins a voice channel, it will show up here.
voice.privacy: Metadata only: audio is never recorded or stored.
voice.ignoredHelp: Click a channel to exclude it (it gets crossed out). Join/leave notices go in Logs → Voice.
voice.noVoice: This server has no voice channels.
voice.noticesHelp: Where NEXUS posts voice joins and leaves (set in Logs → Voice).

honeypot.description: A trap channel people don't use but spam bots do: whoever writes there is sanctioned and what they sent in other channels is deleted.
honeypot.how1: A channel is created (e.g. #honeypot) with a notice: "don't write here". People can react, but not write.
honeypot.how2: People read the notice and don't write. Spam bots, which paste their message in every channel, fall in.
honeypot.how3: NEXUS deletes that message and what that account sent in other channels in the last minutes.
honeypot.how4: It applies the sanction you choose and alerts staff with what they wrote. The owner, staff and exempt roles can write without sanction.
honeypot.channelHelp: Must be visible and let @everyone write: if nobody can write, bots can't fall in either.
honeypot.created: Trap channel created and notice published.
honeypot.exempt: Roles that can write without sanction
honeypot.exemptHelp: The owner and anyone with Manage Messages are already exempt.
honeypot.actionTitle: What to do with whoever writes
honeypot.actionHelp: Most are hacked accounts or bots: banning is most effective. Timeout is the most cautious.
honeypot.purge: Also delete what they sent in other channels
honeypot.purgeHelp: Looks in every text channel for that account's messages.
honeypot.banPurges: With ban and softban, Discord automatically deletes all their messages from the last day.
honeypot.staffNote: Tip: put the channel at the very top, without a category, so bots find it first. If you applied the verification restriction, keep it among the visible channels.
honeypot.messageHelp: The message people will see. Make it clear so nobody writes by mistake.
honeypot.repeatHelp: Stronger sanctions for whoever writes several times in the trap channel.
honeypot.noSteps: No rules: the same sanction always applies. Add one, e.g. "from the 3rd time → Ban".
honeypot.dupStep: There's already a rule for that time.
honeypot.windowHelp: Only times within this period count.
honeypot.repeatNote: With kick or ban the account leaves the server: it only falls again if it comes back. Rules make most sense with "Delete only" or "Timeout" as the first sanction.

start.title: First steps
start.allDone: All set! Your server is protected and configured.
start.perms_title: Give NEXUS the permissions it needs
start.perms_help: Without them some features won't do anything. Diagnostics tells you which are missing.
start.logs_help: Where deleted messages, joins, sanctions, voice… are reported.
start.welcome_help: A message when someone joins the server.
start.verify_help: Captcha on join and, optionally, hide channels until verified.
start.honeypot_help: Catches spam bots and deletes what they sent in other channels.
start.staff_help: Let moderators view or edit only the modules you choose.

responses.description: Tags posted with /tag, automatic replies when someone writes certain words, and messages pinned to the bottom of a channel.
responses.tagsHelp: Saved texts: /tag rules posts the "rules" text. Great for FAQs.
responses.noTagsBody: Create one for rules, links or answers you repeat often.
responses.triggersHelp: When someone writes certain words, NEXUS replies on its own.
responses.noTriggersBody: For example: if someone asks "how do I verify", explain it.
responses.keywordsHelp: Comma separated. Case and accents don't matter.
responses.match_word: If it contains the whole word or phrase
responses.match_starts: If the message starts like that
responses.match_exact: Only if the message is exactly that
responses.responseHelp: You can use variables like '{'user'}' or '{'server'}'.
responses.stickyHelp: A message that always stays at the bottom of the channel: when people write, NEXUS moves it back down.
responses.noStickyBody: Useful to remind the rules of a trading or reports channel.

counters.description: Locked voice channels at the very top showing live numbers, like "👥 Members: 1,420".
counters.listHelp: Up to 10. '{'count'}' is replaced by the number.
counters.howTo: "Create channels" creates a "📊 Stats" category at the top with one voice channel per counter. Nobody can join them: they only show the number.
counters.limit: Discord only allows renaming a channel twice every 10 minutes, so numbers update every 10 minutes.

events.description: Create events with Going / Maybe / Can't go buttons. Everyone sees the time in their own zone, gets a DM before it starts, and sign-ups are pinged when it begins.
events.title: Title
events.imageHelp: An https://… link, or upload an image with the button (saved in «Images»).
events.noneBody: Create one here or with /event create in Discord.
events.cancelBody: The event card will be marked as cancelled and there will be no reminder.
events.managersHelp: Besides staff with "Manage Events" or "Manage Server".

media.title: Server images
media.help: Upload images to use in your embeds. NEXUS attaches them when sending, so they never expire.
media.drop: Click or drag an image here
media.formats: PNG, JPG, GIF or WEBP · max {max}
media.badType: Only PNG, JPG, GIF or WEBP images are allowed.
media.confirmDelete: Delete this image? Messages already sent keep it, but templates using it will stop showing it.
media.pageDescription: The images you uploaded for your embeds: where they're used and how much space they take.
media.autoCleanup: Images not used by any setting are deleted automatically {days} days after upload (messages already sent keep them in Discord).
media.unusedNow: Right now {count, plural, one {# is unused} other {# are unused}} ({size}).
media.emptyBody: Upload one here or from the image button in any message editor.
media.cleanupBody: {count, plural, one {# image} other {# images}} ({size}) not used by any setting will be deleted. Messages already sent keep them in Discord. If one is in an unsaved embed editor draft, you'll need to upload it again.
media.cleaned: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing to delete} one {# image deleted} other {# images deleted}}
media.confirmDeleteUsed: This image is used in: {places}. If you delete it, those messages will be sent without it. Messages already sent keep it.
media.modeLabel: What to do with the image
media.oneOffHelp: The image is sent only with this message and takes no space in NEXUS (Discord keeps its copy inside the message). If you reload the page before sending, you'll need to pick it again. Max 10 MB in total per message.
